text.p: ReliaStar Financial and Security-Connecticut Corp said Monday they signed a definitive agreement to combine the two companies by merging Security-Connecticut into ReliaStar.
The stock-for-stock transaction is valued at $488 million, which includes ReliaStar's assumption of $75 million of Security-Connecticut debt.

The agreement provides for Security-Connecticut holders to receive a fraction of a share of ReliaStar common stock. This would be calculated by dividing $47 by the average closing price of ReliaStar common stock during a period of 20 trading days ending six business days prior to closing, provided the average closing price of ReliaStar common stock during the 20-day period remained between $52.65 and $60.65.
After the close of the merger, Security-Connecticut's two subsidiaries, Security-Connecticut Life Insurance Co and Lincoln Security Life Insurance Co, would become part of ReliaStar Financial.

Based on the closing price of $59.25 for ReliaStar common stock on February 21, Security-Connecticut shareholders would receive 0.7932 of a share of ReliaStar common stock for each share of Security-Connecticut common stock.

Based on that price, ReliaStar would issue approximately seven million additional shares of common stock, and the total value of the transaction would be about $488 million, including $75 million in debt assumption.
The actual number of shares to be issued in the transaction would be determined at closing.
ReliaStar said it will recommend that its board of directors approve a buyback of ReliaStar common stock of up to $100 million in conjunction with the transaction.
The agreement also includes a breakup provision that would result in a payment of $8 million to ReliaStar under certain circumstances if the transaction were not completed.
Completion of the merger is subject to normal closing conditions, including approval by Security-Connecticut shareholders and various regulatory approvals.
The transaction would be recorded as a purchase. The exchange of shares would be tax-free to Security-Connecticut.

Ronald Jarvis, Security-Connecticut chairman, would continue to serve as chief executive officer of Security- Connecticut Life Insurance Co. Jarvis would be a member of the boards of directors of ReliaStar Life Insurance Co and ReliaStar Bankers Security Life Insurance Co, two wholly owned subsidiaries of ReliaStar Financial Corp. He also would be part of the ReliaStar Management Committee.
John Turner would remain chairman and chief executive officer of ReliaStar Financial Corp.

ReliaStar said that it expects the merger would be essentially non-dilutive to earnings per share in 1997, and accretive to earnings per share in 1998 and beyond, assuming the $100 million buyback of ReliaStar stock in 1997.
The integration of operations following the merger would result in anticipated combined net pre-tax annualized expense reductions of at least $7 million.
